## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks the correctness gaps only on a bare plan — completeness gaps below stay informational until a detail bundle exists. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply roadmap-immutable-evidence-storage   # walk + apply each correctness gap
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk roadmap-immutable-evidence-storage  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[first-use-directory-race]`: Step 1’s Architecture treats a namespace directory created by another live publisher as “pre-existing” and usable as-is, but only the creator syncs each new directory with its parent. A second first-use call can create lower components and return `created` or `existing` before `.plan-tool` is synced into the configured roadmap directory; the Reduced-scope fence’s “exclusive create resolves the only real race,” the first-use host-failure Risk, Testing’s directory-order check, and acceptance criterion 1 then fail their returned-byte durability promise.
  - Fix: define concurrent first-use ownership so every publisher establishes the fixed directory ancestry’s required durability boundaries before it returns final bytes, and cover competing initializers in the ordering tests and criterion
- HIGH `[macos-directory-durability]`: Step 1 (`Add minimal immutable evidence publication and enumeration helper`) runs macOS `F_FULLFSYNC` on the temporary before linking the final, then uses only `fsync` for the namespace directory after the link. The cited [Apple fsync reference](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/fsync.2.html) says ordinary `fsync` can leave writes in the drive cache, so the Architecture, host-failure Risk, Testing’s macOS check, and acceptance criterion 3 can acknowledge `created`, `existing`, or listed bytes while the final name still disappears after a power loss.
  - Fix: Define and test a macOS full-storage boundary after the final directory synchronization for every path that returns final bytes, including created, existing, and enumeration results.
- HIGH `[case-folded-final-name]`: Step 1’s `EEXIST` loser path assumes lookup preserves the exact lowercase final name. On a case-insensitive macOS volume, an uppercase 64-hex entry makes the lowercase link fail and can be read as `existing`, while Architecture’s final-name grammar and enumeration, the Reduced-scope fence, the unrelated-entry Risk, Testing’s competing/non-matching cases, and acceptance criteria 2, 5, and 6 require non-matching names to remain non-evidence; enumeration can then omit bytes publication returned.
  - Fix: Require an exact raw-name check before returning `existing`, classify a case-folded non-matching collision as `write-failed`, and test case-insensitive lookup semantics.
